name: Office Opening Checklist
description: A step-by-step routine for opening the office safely and smoothly every morning.

items.text: Approach the building and check the exterior for damage, forced entry or anything out of place before entering.
Unlock the main entrance and any secondary doors required for staff access.
Disarm the security alarm within the allowed time window using your code.
items.note: Keep the monitoring company number handy in case of accidental triggering.

items.text: Confirm CCTV and access control systems are powered and recording.
Prop open or unlock internal doors that staff need throughout the day.
Switch on main lighting in entrances, corridors and shared areas.
Adjust heating or air conditioning to a comfortable temperature for the day.
Turn on shared printers, copiers and scanners and check for paper and toner.
Power up reception screens, signage and any visitor sign-in systems.
Confirm Wi-Fi and the network are online and reachable.
Walk the floor and check that fire exits and walkways are clear and unobstructed.
Look for spills, leaks or trip hazards and address them before staff arrive.
items.note: Place wet-floor signs if cleaning has left surfaces damp.

items.text: Check that emergency exit doors open freely and are not blocked or locked.
Confirm first aid kits are in place and visible.
Note any maintenance issues and log them for follow-up.
Wipe down reception and shared desks if needed and tidy any clutter left overnight.
Switch on the kitchen, fill and start the coffee machine and check the kettle and water dispenser.
Restock the breakroom with milk, tea, coffee and clean mugs.
items.note: Check fridge dates and remove anything spoiled.

items.text: Empty the dishwasher and run any waiting load.
Set out fresh hand towels and refill soap and sanitizer dispensers.
Open blinds or curtains to let in natural light.
Check meeting rooms are clean, chairs are arranged and screens or conferencing kit are working.
Turn on shared monitors, phones and reception equipment.
Bring in and sort any deliveries or post left at the door.
Review the day's calendar for visitors, deliveries or meetings that need setup.
Confirm all systems are running and no error lights or alerts are showing.
Check that the reception area looks welcoming and presentable.
Verify staff entrances are accessible and visitor doors are appropriately secured.
Report any unresolved issues to the office manager or facilities team.
Sign and date the opening log to confirm the routine is complete.

faq.q: Who should be responsible for opening the office?
faq.a: Assign a primary opener and at least one trained backup. Give both the alarm code, keys or fob access, and a copy of this checklist so cover is seamless when the main person is away.

faq.q: How long should opening the office take?
faq.a: Most offices can complete the full routine in 10 to 15 minutes. Building familiarity speeds it up, but never skip the safety scan or alarm steps to save time.

faq.q: What should I do if the alarm goes off by mistake?
faq.a: Stay calm, enter your disarm code, and call the monitoring company with your account password to cancel the dispatch. Keep the password and phone number on a card near the panel.

faq.q: Can I customize this opening checklist for my office?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, then add building-specific steps such as opening shutters, switching on signage, unlocking gates or starting machinery relevant to your workplace.

faq.q: Should the opening checklist be done every day?
faq.a: Yes, run it every business day, including days with reduced staff. A consistent daily routine is what prevents forgotten steps like unlocked doors or systems left offline.
